question: For any strategy, do lifecycles that remain open beyond their entry server date have broadly nonpositive stressed-R, materially worse outcomes and higher stop-loss incidence than same-server-day lifecycles, enough to justify one later entry-preserving server-day-boundary management experiment?

fixed_reconstruction.row_and_order_contract: Preserve each distinct CSV row and use the same verified server_time, state_sequence, event-precedence, source-path and source-line ordering as the closed 016 and 017 diagnostics.
fixed_reconstruction.lifecycle_birth: OPEN begins RC16, RC4, Cross, Pressure and Return; PASSIVE_FILL begins Passive using its paired placement planned_risk.
fixed_reconstruction.lifecycle_release: CLOSE or EXTERNAL_CLOSE supplies close server time, native stressed net and stop-loss reason.
fixed_reconstruction.SAME_DAY: close server calendar date equals entry server calendar date
fixed_reconstruction.CARRY: close server calendar date is strictly later than entry server calendar date
fixed_reconstruction.carry_days: integer difference between close and entry server calendar dates; descriptive above one day
fixed_reconstruction.stressed_r: native stressed net USD divided by birth planned_risk
fixed_reconstruction.pooled_r_effect: CARRY mean stressed_r minus SAME_DAY mean stressed_r
fixed_reconstruction.period_r_effect: The same difference within each period
fixed_reconstruction.pooled_stop_effect: CARRY stop-loss rate minus SAME_DAY stop-loss rate
fixed_reconstruction.period_stop_effect: The same stop-rate difference within each period

causal_limit.observable_time: CARRY status becomes causally knowable only when the entry server date boundary is crossed while the position remains open.
causal_limit.not_claimed: This diagnostic does not know the mark or executable close result at that boundary and therefore cannot itself establish that closing there improves P/L.
causal_limit.later_test_if_selected: A later real-tick EA must compare native continuation with an exact server-day-boundary action and retain the unchanged entry path.

fixed_integrity_gate: All 2,233 lifecycles, 407.0477 USD stressed net and 206 stop exits reconstruct exactly with no duplicate, pairing, overlap, risk or time fault.
Every close time is at or after entry time and every carry_days value is nonnegative.
Every lifecycle belongs to exactly one SAME_DAY or CARRY group.

requirements: SAME_DAY and CARRY each contain at least 20 pooled lifecycles.
Each group contains at least five lifecycles in at least three periods.
Pooled CARRY mean stressed_r is nonpositive.
Pooled CARRY-minus-SAME_DAY mean stressed_r is at most -0.10R per lifecycle.
Among periods with at least five observations in both groups, at least three period stressed-R effects are negative.
CARRY mean stressed_r is nonpositive in at least three periods.
Pooled CARRY-minus-SAME_DAY stop-loss-rate difference is at least +0.10.
Among periods with at least five observations in both groups, at least three period stop-rate effects are positive.
fixed_information_gate.selection: Select at most one passing strategy by more negative pooled stressed-R effect, then larger positive stop effect, then more negative-effect periods, then lexicographic name.
fixed_information_gate.passing_action: Retain one later real-tick server-day-boundary management experiment for the selected strategy. It must preserve all base entries, retain unchanged 4%/12% admission and remain Lab-only.
fixed_information_gate.failure_action: Close with no carry-management candidate. Do not rescue with local-day boundary, broker rollover minute, weekday, multi-day threshold, swap sign, direction, symbol or strategy-specific time exception.

descriptive_only: swap fields from the MT5 report
stop_rules: Run exactly one successful fixed aggregation; disclose implementation-only failures before judgment.
Do not run MT5 or modify MQL in this unit.
Do not infer boundary-close profitability from native final outcomes alone.
Do not alter, query or restart Live.
